statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). Globex equity futures reopened at 22:00 UTC and NQ gapped roughly 1.2% lower as the weekend AI-pacing story priced in, but the first half hour has traded two-way inside a band of about 120 points with an observed bounce off the low, so Tail stays in the watch band rather than the block band. Stress stays high because crude gained more than 3% after Hormuz de-escalation talks were postponed, and the FOMC decision is on Wednesday.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: 22:00-01:00 UTC, covering the reopen repricing and the thin stretch before Tokyo engages. A secondary checkpoint sits at the 13:30 UTC US cash open on Monday, where the forecast re-enters the watch band for the first full cash hour before decaying again.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopen about 1.2% lower as the AI-pacing story prices in and Hormuz talks are postponed, but the first half hour trades two-way
body: Live price-path evidence exists again. CME equity futures reopened at 22:00 UTC and NQ is quoted near 29,032.50, down 354.50 or 1.21%, having opened at 28,997.75 and traded a 28,981.00-29,100.00 band as of 18:15 EDT. Investing.com independently shows the contract down 1.24% against a 29,684.25 prior close. The structure inside that gap is the material point: price reached 28,981, recovered about 119 points to 29,100 and settled back near the middle of the range. That is a real retracement and two-way discovery, not repeated extension after failed pullbacks, which is why the reopen has not pushed Tail toward the blocking band. The move is also sector-specific rather than systemic. ES is down 0.61% against NQ's 1.21%, so the Nasdaq is underperforming by roughly two to one, consistent with a technology and semiconductor repricing of the weekend AI-pacing story rather than broad de-risking. Cross-assets are unaligned, which normally argues for Stress over Tail: the 10-year note future is bid at 106.21875, up 0.10%, so yields are marginally lower rather than confirming an inflation shock; gold is down 0.86% at 4,371.20, which a systemic flight to safety would not produce. The energy leg did change over the weekend. WTI is up 3.08% near $103.13 after trading 101.59-103.33, and the reason is verified: Oman postponed Monday's Salalah meeting between Iran and Gulf states on a temporary Hormuz shipping lane, with Bahrain's refusal to attend cited behind the decision. The prior assessment treated that meeting as a two-sided de-escalation checkpoint; it is now removed rather than resolved. Alongside it, reporting describes US strikes on Iranian minelaying assets at Larak Island, Houthi capture of Mokha and Mayyun Island in the Bab el-Mandeb, and a precautionary shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline after attacks. That is a genuine supply-side escalation and it is the main reason Stress rises rather than falls. The rates and policy backdrop is unchanged from the pre-reopen assessment: the 10-year near 4.95% and the 2-year near 4.56% on the latest H.15, with reporting that the 2-year touched 4.596% on Friday, and CME FedWatch showing an 85.6% probability of a quarter-point hike at Wednesday's FOMC with the press conference half an hour after the decision. Friday's cash session closed risk-on, with the Nasdaq-100 up 0.91% at 29,368.44 and VIX down 11.21% to 15.84, so tonight's gap is a reversal of that tone rather than a continuation of it. Shared cross-asset context collected at 21:48 UTC is pre-reopen and therefore describes Friday: seven of eight megacaps higher, semiconductors averaging plus 1.75%, and positive technology and communication-services breadth. It is used only as confirmation of the starting point, not as evidence of the current path. The net reading is an event-driven gap that is so far being absorbed, against a backdrop that has become harder. Tail sits at 22 in the watch band, Stress at 78, and the danger window is narrowed to the three hours in which the reopen repricing and the thinnest liquidity of the week overlap.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and the dominant mode was normal throughout. Tail held at 6 through the overnight hours, drifted up from 05:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, reached 17 by 15:00 UTC, and stepped through 16, 17, 18, 18, 19 and 21 across the final six hours as the reopen approached. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 23 hours and moved to WATCH and yellow in the final hour. Stress rose steadily from 56 to 77 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, while Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to the low 70s from 16:00 UTC as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The overnight window splits into two phases. The concentrated conditional risk sits in the 22:00-01:00 UTC stretch, where the observed reopen gap is still being priced in the thinnest liquidity of the week and Tokyo has not yet engaged; the specific invalidation is a decisive break of the 28,981 reopen low with shallow or failed pullbacks, and Tail peaks at 22 there rather than in the block band because the first retracement has already occurred. From the Tokyo open onward the base case is continued absorption, with Tail decaying toward 15 through the European morning. Two later checkpoints follow: the 07:00 UTC European cash open, the first deep cash market to price the AI-pacing story, and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where the forecast re-enters the watch band for the first full cash hour before decaying again. Monday's US calendar holds only routine 3-month and 6-month bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, so residual daytime risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel now that the Salalah Iran-GCC meeting has been postponed rather than held. Stress stays in the high band across the whole window because none of the underlying tension resolves before Wednesday: a hike priced near 85.6%, a 10-year close to 5%, crude above $100 with a Saudi pipeline shut, and an AI-pacing debate that has only had one thin session to price.

The gap has already been bought off the low and given back, so discovery is two-way rather than one-way. Tail eases below the 24 allowance carried for this hour.
